intents.description: Closes (unloads) an application by its ID from the dock.

required.description: The unique identifier of the application to close.

required.name: applicationId
required.description: The unique identifier of the application to check.

Checks whether an application with the given ID is currently loaded (open) in the dock.

services.title: Application Service
services.description: Issues short-lived signed identity JWTs for iFrame (mini-app) applications. Allows an embedded application to obtain a signed token proving the current user's identity to the mini-app's own backend.

intents.description: Issues a short-lived signed identity JWT for the calling mini-app. The target application is inferred from the intent sender — no parameters needed. Requires the user to be authenticated. JWT claims: sub=userId, aud=callingApplicationId, iss=platform, exp=5min.
Closes all currently loaded applications and clears all docks. Unlike the normal close flow, does not re-open the default application — the UI stays blank with no application displayed.

Expands the calling application to fill the dock by closing every other loaded application. The target application is inferred from the intent sender — no parameters needed. Mirrors the "Expand Application" default header action for iframe apps that render their own context menu (header: false).

Closes the calling application (unloads it from its dock), then re-opens the default network application if nothing is left docked. The target application is inferred from the intent sender — no parameters needed. Mirrors the "Close Application" default header action for iframe apps that render their own context menu (header: false).

required.name: targetType

intents.description: Lists every badge visible to the current user — badges scoped to their networks plus global ones. Use this to resolve a badge name to the badgeId required by search-users-by-badge-id and the policy intents.

optional.name: offset
optional.description: Pagination offset. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: size
optional.description: Number of results to return. Defaults to 10.

intents.description: Opens a file picker over the Network Resources of the current network so a network admin can choose ONE file, and waits for the choice. The popup opens over whatever is on screen and does not open Media. BLOCKS until the user picks or cancels. Returns the picked resource `{id, title, contentType, thumbnailUrl}` or `null` when the user cancels or closes the popup. Refused (an error, and no popup) for anyone who is not an admin of the network, for an unknown source, and for a folderId outside the requested sources. The returned resource is always inside the requested sources.

required.name: sources
required.description: Where files may be picked from. Only "networkResources" (the public files of the network, `networkPublic:{networkId}`) is supported. Nothing outside these sources is shown or reachable.

optional.name: accept
optional.description: File types that can be picked: a family ("image"), a family wildcard ("image/*") or an exact type ("image/png"). Other files are shown disabled. Omit to allow any file.

optional.name: folderId
optional.description: Folder to open in. Must be a folder inside the requested sources, otherwise the call is refused.

optional.name: title
optional.description: Popup title. Defaults to "Choose a file".

services.title: Commerce
services.description: Products, the cart, orders and the seller's own store, shared across apps. An app shows the network's products and adds them to the one cart the user pays for with a single QR scan, and it can run the signed-in seller's store: products, publishing, promotions and analytics. Prices, totals and payouts are decided server-side. Paying is never an action here: `checkout` hands the buyer to My Cart, where they press Pay and scan the code themselves, and answers with what they did. A write that costs the user money, gives goods away, cannot be undone or speaks for them in public waits for their yes in a dialog the platform draws.

intents.description: Search the live products available in the user's current network — the buyer's shelf, every seller's goods, not only yours. Products the network or its admins have refused are simply absent from the answer. Each product names its seller, who is a PERSON, not a store: `sellerName` (their profile name), `sellerUserId` (draw their avatar with the users API's getIcon({userId: sellerUserId})) and `sellerIdentityName` (the Verus ID payments go to). `storeName` carries the same person's name, for older callers; show the person, never a store. For the signed-in seller's OWN products, drafts included, use list-seller-products.

optional.name: query
optional.description: free-text search over the product title, or a whole tag

optional.name: storeId
optional.description: only this seller's products: a product's `storeId`, from list-products or get-product. Every user has one store, so this is everything one person sells (My Cart's "Everything from this store")

optional.name: category
optional.description: one of the platform's category ids — see list-categories

optional.name: tag
optional.description: one tag, matched exactly (case and spacing do not matter)

optional.name: attributes
optional.description: app-defined facets to filter by, e.g. {"subject": "Mathematics"}

optional.name: sort
optional.description: newest | popular | priceAsc | priceDesc | rating

optional.name: limit
optional.description: page size, up to 100 (default 24)

optional.name: offset
optional.description: where the page starts

intents.description: One product with its price, its parts when it is a bundle, its seller, its reviews and whether the current user already owns it. The seller is a PERSON, as in list-products: `sellerName`, `sellerUserId` (their avatar through the users API's getIcon) and `sellerIdentityName`; the store record's name is that person too. `contents` is what the product holds, as a tree to draw: `{type: "folder", title, items}`, `{type: "file", resourceId, title, kind, contentType, fileSize}` and `{type: "product", productId, title}`. `children` is NOT the content: it is only the products a bundle includes, empty for anything else. `items` is the same content as flat database rows, kept for older callers. A file's `resourceId` (and `resource_id` in items) is null unless the user owns the product or sells it: titles and types are the shop window, the ids open the paid files. For something the user bought, use get-purchase-contents.

required.name: productId
required.description: the product to read

intents.description: The platform's product categories as `{categories: [{id, label}]}`. Every product is filed under exactly one; pass an `id` to list-products as `category`, and show the `label`.
Put a product in the user's cart, credited to your app. The server re-checks that it can be bought here before accepting it, so a refusal comes back with a code to show.

required.name: productId
required.description: the product to add

optional.name: qty
optional.description: how many, at least 1 (default 1)

intents.description: Which of these products the current user owns. This is how an app unlocks a ticket, a seat or an in-app good it sold through the shared cart.

required.name: productIds
required.description: the product ids to check

intents.description: Reads the user's cart — every item in it, from every app, as the buyer will check it out. Returns `{items, count}` where `count` excludes anything saved for later. Use it to show a badge, a summary, or to tell whether something this app sells is already in there. Each item's `appId` says which app added it. An app changes only its own rows: `add-to-cart` adds one, `update-cart-item` changes one, `remove-from-cart` and `clear-cart` take them out. Every other app's items are the buyer's to change in My Cart: send them there with `open-cart`.

Create a product for the seller, as a DRAFT. Two ways in. With no params it opens the platform's own 'list something for sale' form in a modal and BLOCKS until the seller creates a product or cancels. With a `title` it creates the draft directly from the fields given — name, description, price, category, tags, cover and content — without a form: use this when you already have the resource ids (a generated cover, files found in Media). Either way returns `{success: true, product}` (or `{success: false, product: null, code}`; `cancelled` when the seller backed out of the form), and the product is already in the seller's catalogue. It is NEVER published here: publishing decides money and networks, so the seller confirms it separately — in the publish dialog an app opens with publish-product, or in the Merchant Console. Opening a store first (a verified Verus identity) is handled inside.

optional.name: title
optional.description: the product's name; giving one creates the draft directly instead of opening the form

optional.name: description
optional.description: what a buyer reads before paying

optional.name: priceAmount
optional.description: the price; 0 or omitted is a free product. When items include other products, this is the price ON TOP of theirs

optional.name: priceCurrency
optional.description: VRSC (default) or USD

optional.name: category
optional.description: one of the platform's category ids — see list-categories; required before the seller can publish

optional.name: tags
optional.description: up to 10 tags of up to 24 characters; normalised (lowercase, trimmed)

optional.name: imageResourceId
optional.description: the cover: a resource id in the seller's own Media, e.g. one you generated

optional.name: items
optional.description: the content a buyer receives: resource ids ("res_1"), named files ({resourceId, title}), folders ({folder: "Unit 1", items: […]}) or other products ({productId}) for a bundle

optional.name: stock
optional.description: how many may be sold; omit for unlimited

intents.description: Every product the SIGNED-IN user sells, from their own store, so an app can show a seller their own products: live, draft (unlisted ones included), archived and broken, in every network, including ones a network blocked. Unlike list-products, the buyer's shelf of live products allowed here. The store is always the current user's; there is no way to name another. Read-only, newest change first. Returns `{hasStore, products}`; `hasStore` is false (and products empty) when the user has no store. Each product: id, title, description, status, category, tags, priceAmount, priceCurrency, totalPriceAmount, isBundle, coverResourceId, stock (null = unlimited), soldCount, contentCount. Show totalPriceAmount as the price: on a bundle priceAmount is only the seller's part on top of what it includes, and totalPriceAmount is null when the server could not price the bundle.

optional.name: status
optional.description: only products in this state

optional.name: limit
optional.description: how many to return: 100 by default, up to 500

intents.description: List the SELLER's own products in their store — drafts, unlisted, live and archived — unlike list-products, which is the buyer's shelf and never shows drafts. Use it to find the productId to edit. Each product carries `editable`: true only for a draft (never published, or unlisted by the seller). Returns `{hasStore, products}`.

optional.name: status
optional.description: only products in this state

optional.name: limit
optional.description: how many to return

intents.description: One of the seller's own products with its content, in exactly the shape update-product takes: `{product, items}`. Read it before changing the content — `items` in update-product REPLACES the whole tree, so edit this list and send it back rather than sending only the new files. `product.editable` is true for a draft, whose fields and content may change; a `broken` product (needs attention: something it included was archived) takes new content only.

required.name: productId
required.description: the product, from list-seller-products (an app) or list-my-products (the AI)

intents.description: Edit one of the seller's own DRAFT products — one never published, or one the seller unlisted. A live or archived product is refused with code `not_editable` (a live one must be unlisted first: unlist-product, or the seller in the Merchant Console). A `broken` product (needs attention: something it included was archived) accepts `items` only — its other fields are `not_editable` — and goes back on sale when it is published again (publish-product). Only the fields given change. `items` REPLACES the content: call get-my-product first and send back the edited list; an empty list is refused. Never publishes. Returns `{success: true, product}` or `{success: false, code, error}`.

required.name: productId
required.description: the draft (or broken product) to edit, from list-seller-products (an app) or list-my-products (the AI)

optional.name: title
optional.description: the product's name

optional.name: description
optional.description: what a buyer reads before paying; an empty string clears it

optional.name: priceAmount
optional.description: the price; 0 makes it free. On a product that includes other products this is the price ON TOP of theirs (a buyer pays the included products plus this)

optional.name: priceCurrency
optional.description: VRSC or USD

optional.name: stock
optional.description: how many may be sold (the quantity on sale)

optional.name: unlimitedStock
optional.description: true removes the quantity limit

optional.name: category
optional.description: one of the platform's category ids — see list-categories; an empty string clears it

optional.name: tags
optional.description: the full tag list (replaces the current one): up to 10 tags of up to 24 characters

optional.name: imageResourceId
optional.description: the cover: a resource id in the seller's own Media

optional.name: items
optional.description: the WHOLE new content: resource ids ("res_1"), named files ({resourceId, title}), folders ({folder: "Unit 1", items: […]}) or other products ({productId}) for a bundle

intents.description: What the signed-in user OWNS — every product they bought, wherever they bought it, as My Cart's Orders tab lists it. Returns `{purchases: [{productId, title, coverResourceId, purchasedAt, orderId, boughtInAppId, isBundlePart, delivered, deletedBySeller, progress}]}`. `delivered` is true once the buyer's own copy is in their Media; `isBundlePart` marks a product that came inside a bundle; a purchase the seller deleted is still theirs. `progress` is `{openedFiles, totalFiles, complete}` — how many of its files the user has opened (a bundle counts its parts); `complete` marks a purchase read to the end. Null when unknown.

optional.name: thisAppOnly
optional.description: true lists only what was bought in YOUR app

intents.description: One purchase opened up: the version the user BOUGHT (frozen at purchase, not the product as it is now), as a tree to draw. Returns `{productId, title, deletedBySeller, contents, progress}`; contents nodes are `{type: "folder", title, items}`, `{type: "file", resourceId, title, kind, contentType, fileSize, deliveredResourceId, seen}` and `{type: "product", productId, title}` (a product inside a bundle — open it with its own get-purchase-contents). `deliveredResourceId` is the buyer's own copy in Media, null until delivered. `seen` is true once the user has opened that file (draw a green check — bought products are often lessons); a file whose `kind` is "folder" has no `seen`. `progress` is `{openedFiles, totalFiles, complete}` (a bundle counts its parts; `complete` once every file is opened), null when unknown. Refused with code `not_owned` when the user does not own the product — the server decides.

required.name: productId
required.description: a product the user owns, from list-purchases

intents.description: Open the platform's previewer on what the user bought — the Orders tab's click on a file. It holds every file of the purchase in tree order, with previous / next arrows between them, and opens on `resourceId` when given (it must be in the purchase: its `resourceId` or `deliveredResourceId` from get-purchase-contents), on the first file otherwise. Every file the user lands on is marked as opened (`seen` in get-purchase-contents). A folder resource is shown on its own. Returns `{success: true, count}`, or `{success: false, code}` with `not_owned`, `not_in_purchase` or `empty`. The previewer is a window over the whole page.

required.name: productId
required.description: a product the user owns

optional.name: resourceId
optional.description: the file of that purchase to open on

intents.description: Mark one of the user's purchased files as OPENED, for an app that shows a purchase's files itself (preview-purchase marks the files it shows by itself). The file must be in the purchase (its `resourceId` or `deliveredResourceId` from get-purchase-contents) and not a folder. Returns `{success: true, resourceId, progress}` — `progress` as in get-purchase-contents — or `{success: false, code}` with `not_owned` or `not_in_purchase`.

required.name: productId
required.description: a product the user owns

required.name: resourceId
required.description: the file of that purchase the user opened

intents.description: Open a purchase where it lives, in Media's Purchased section — the Orders tab's "Show in Media". The buyer's delivered folder when there is one, otherwise a read-only view of the version they bought. Without `productId`, the whole Purchased section. Media docks beside your app. Returns `{success: true}`, or `{success: false, code: "not_owned"}` without opening anything.

optional.name: productId
optional.description: a product the user owns; omit for everything they bought

intents.description: Open My Cart for the user, scoped to your app's items. With `popup` it is drawn over your own app instead of docking My Cart — mid-purchase, that keeps the user where they were. It answers as soon as the cart is open; for a Pay button use `checkout`, which opens the same cart and answers with what the buyer did there.

optional.name: popup
optional.description: true draws the surface over YOUR app's own pane instead of docking the application, so the page the user was on stays visible and usable behind it. Where your app is not on screen it falls back to a window over the whole page.

intents.description: Open what the user OWNS in My Cart's Purchased tab — each product with its files, how far through them they are, and their rating; with `productId`, that product opened and shown. Receipts are `open-order`. With `popup` it is drawn over your own app instead of docking My Cart.

optional.name: productId
optional.description: a product the user owns, to open and show

optional.name: popup
optional.description: true draws the surface over YOUR app's own pane instead of docking the application, so the page the user was on stays visible and usable behind it. Where your app is not on screen it falls back to a window over the whole page.

intents.description: Open the seller's own products in the Merchant Console — the seller's side of `open-cart`. Use it for a "My products" link: it shows everything they sell across every app, not just yours, and whether they may sell at all is the platform's decision, not your app's. With `popup` it is drawn over your own app instead of docking the console.

optional.name: popup
optional.description: true draws the surface over YOUR app's own pane instead of docking the application, so the page the user was on stays visible and usable behind it. Where your app is not on screen it falls back to a window over the whole page.

intents.description: Change one of YOUR app's rows in the user's cart: its quantity, whether it is selected for checkout, or whether it is saved for later. Give at least one of them; only the fields given change. A row added by another app is refused with code `not_yours` — the buyer changes those in My Cart (`open-cart`) — and a row the cart does not hold with `not_found`. Returns the whole cart as get-cart reads it: `{success: true, items, count}`, `count` excluding what is saved for later. The server re-checks stock and availability and refuses with its own code.

required.name: itemId
required.description: the cart row to change: an item `id` from get-cart, one your app added

optional.name: qty
optional.description: the new quantity, a whole number of at least 1

optional.name: selected
optional.description: true to include it in the next checkout, false to leave it out

optional.name: savedForLater
optional.description: true moves it out of the cart into saved for later; false brings it back

intents.description: Take one of YOUR app's rows out of the user's cart. Another app's row is refused with code `not_yours` (the buyer removes those in My Cart), a row the cart does not hold with `not_found`. Returns the whole cart: `{success: true, items, count}`.

required.name: itemId
required.description: the cart row to remove: an item `id` from get-cart, one your app added

intents.description: Remove every row YOUR app added to the user's cart, saved-for-later ones included. Other apps' rows are never touched. No dialog: they are your own rows. Returns what is left — `{success: true, items, count}` — so an empty `items` means the cart held only your rows.

What a discount code would do to the items YOUR app has selected in the cart — exactly what `checkout` will charge for them. Returns `{valid, reason, discounts: [{kind, label, amountVrsc}], subtotalVrsc, totalVrsc}`. `reason` is null when valid, else `promo_invalid`, `promo_expired`, `promo_exhausted` or `not_applicable` (a real code that takes nothing off this selection, e.g. under its minimum). `discounts` lists everything that takes money off, the code and any volume discount or sale alike. Read-only: nothing is reserved, and My Cart prices the code again when the buyer pays. With nothing of yours selected the server refuses `validation_failed`.

required.name: code
required.description: the code as the buyer typed it; case and surrounding spaces do not matter

intents.description: How this network SHOWS prices: `{currency, vrscUsd}`, where `currency` is `USD` or `VRSC` (the network admins' choice) and `vrscUsd` is the server's VRSC→USD rate, null when it is unknown. Every amount Commerce answers with stays in VRSC (`…Vrsc`); multiply by `vrscUsd` to show dollars, and show VRSC when the rate is null.

Your app's Pay button. Your app never takes a payment: this opens My Cart's own cart over your app, showing your items with `promoCode` typed in and applied, and the BUYER presses Pay and scans the code there — only My Cart creates the order. It answers when the buyer closes it: `{success: true, outcome, orderId?, status?}`. `outcome` is `paid` (a free order too: unlock it), `pending` (an order was made but is not paid yet — follow it with get-order or the order-updated event), `cancelled` (the order will not be paid: the buyer cancelled it, or it expired or failed — `status` says which — and its items are back in the cart) or `dismissed` (closed without making an order). Refused with code `empty`, and nothing opens, when none of your items is selected in the cart (add them first). With `popup: false` My Cart docks instead and it answers at once with `outcome: "opened"`, as it does where there is no popup to draw. A second checkout while one is open replaces it; the first answers at once — `dismissed`, unless an order was already made in it.

optional.name: promoCode
optional.description: a discount code to type in and apply for the buyer; check it first with preview-promo

optional.name: popup
optional.description: false docks My Cart instead of drawing its cart over your app (default true)

intents.description: Open one of the user's orders in My Cart, expanded: where the buyer resumes a pending payment ("Show code"), cancels or deletes an unpaid order, or reads a receipt. intents.description: The store's own numbers over a range — the Merchant Console's Analytics — exactly as the server sends them: `{range, totals: {revenueVrsc, orders, units, curatorFeeVrsc, revenueApproximate}, series: [{day, revenueVrsc, orders, suppressed}], topProducts: [{productId, title, revenueVrsc, units, suppressed}], byNetwork: [{networkId, revenueVrsc, orders, suppressed}], suppressedCells}`. A row with `suppressed: true` was built from too few orders and is WITHHELD: its numbers are not figures — show it as withheld, never as 0. `orders` counts order lines touched, an upper bound, not distinct orders. Read-only.

optional.name: to
optional.description: ISO date the range ends

optional.description: true reads the test orders' figures instead of the real ones (never mixed)

intents.description: Be told when commerce changes instead of polling. Name the events you want; the answer is `{success: true, events}`, your app's whole set now: each call REPLACES the previous one, and an empty list stops them all. An unknown name is refused with `validation_failed` and nothing changes; a caller that is not an embedded app is refused with `unsupported`. Each event arrives as a host push, `api:trigger` with `{action: "commerce", data: {event, …}}` (the SDK emits `ValuApi.ON_COMMERCE` with that `data`). The events and their data: `cart-updated {count}` — the cart changed; `count` is what the cart badge shows (saved-for-later excluded), never which items: re-read with get-cart. `order-updated {orderId, status}` — an order holding at least one of YOUR app's items changed: pending_payment, paid, failed, expired, cancelled or deleted. Orders without your items are never sent to you. `delivery-updated {orderId, status}` — that order's files: delivered (they are in the buyer's Media; re-read with list-purchases), unavailable or failed. `catalogue-updated {productId, change}` — the shelf of this network changed: change is added, updated or removed; productId null means re-read the whole shelf with list-products. `seller-product-updated {productId, change}` — one of the signed-in seller's own products: created, updated, content-updated, published, unlisted, archived, deleted, broken, sale-started, sale-ended, blocked or unblocked; re-read with list-seller-products. `seller-store-updated {change, networkId?}` — their store: created, updated, donation-updated or network-access-updated (networkId names the network when there is one). `seller-promotions-updated {change}` — a promotion changed: sale, tier or code. An event says WHAT changed, never the new state: treat it as a hint to re-read with the matching intent, never as data, and expect to miss one now and then (a missed event is a stale screen until the next read). Subscriptions last until unsubscribe-events, until your app's frame closes or until it reloads — moving the app to another dock reloads its frame — so subscribe again every time your app starts, after api:ready.

required.description: the event names to receive, replacing any earlier subscription: cart-updated, order-updated, delivery-updated, catalogue-updated, seller-product-updated, seller-store-updated, seller-promotions-updated

intents.description: Stop receiving commerce events. Without `events`, every one your app subscribed to; with it, only those. Answers `{success: true, events}`: what your app still receives (empty when nothing). An unknown name is refused with `validation_failed` and nothing changes. There is no need to call it before your app closes: a subscription ends with the frame that made it.

optional.name: events
optional.description: the event names to stop receiving (see subscribe-events); omit to stop them all

Returns { roomId, name, networkId, tag, price, isFree, paymentRequired } for the NEW room plus, when paymentRequired is true, paymentWindowMinutes (15) and paymentInstructions. When paymentRequired is true you MUST tell the user right away: the price, that the room is temporary until it is bought within 15 minutes, and how to pay (Valu web app -> Rooms -> open the new room -> "Pay for Room"); never claim it is paid. Creating the room and linking to it are two separate steps: to link, paste the returned `tag` (`@[room:networkId/roomId|Name]`) VERBATIM — never rebuild it from ids, never reuse a roomId from an earlier call or a template id, and never guess the networkId. Template placeholder resources still sitting on the prop (from the room template) are removed first so they never mix with the user's content (removedTemplateStubs in the result lists them; set removeTemplateStubs=false to keep them). When the paste leaves more than one resource on a non-container prop, the tool automatically enables the prop's auto content slider so the items cycle as a slideshow (result field sliderEnabled reports it; sliderError appears if the paste succeeded but the slider toggle failed). The tool also CLEARS the prop's title (content props carry no caption — a section's name lives on its sign; titleCleared reports it, titleClearError if that save failed). Use this tool ONLY when the user named exactly one prop. When the target is a GROUP — a row of frames, a tagged section, several props — call paste-resources-into-prop-group instead: it spreads the content across the group's props in navigation order itself, so never hand-split content into per-prop calls. The prop must support content — check via get-room-props that its type array is non-empty and isPresentationBoard is false: presentation (screen-share) boards are rejected, they are reserved for live screen sharing. Prefer props with thumbnailCount > 0 (picture frames / display canvases). Use service__CMS__resource_search to find resource ids first. Returns the paste result plus `name` and `tag` read back AFTER the paste, so they name what the prop now shows (its first resource) — paste that `tag` verbatim when linking to the prop.

Returns { roomId, networkId, propOrder, groupIds, groups } — groupIds is the ordered list of every group id, read it first. A group is the set of props whose normalized tags (lowercase, spaces -> "-") are identical; its `id` is those tags sorted and joined with "+" (e.g. "building1+floor0+team"), so multi-tag rooms yield one group per tag combination ("building1+floor0+team" and "building1+floor1+team" are different groups). A SINGLE tagged prop is a group of one — the lone "logo" frame is the group "logo". Props WITHOUT tags belong to no group and are skipped entirely (never listed, never filled). Each group carries id, tags, label, isLogoGroup (true when the tags include "logo": every logo frame shows EVERY logo, so paste-resources-into-prop-group replicates there by default), navIndex (the group's first position in the room's walk; null = outside it), propCount, eligiblePropCount (props that can take content), decorativePropCount (props with no content type — walls, plants, signs — counted but NOT listed), totalContentCount, labels — the section's SIGNS: Text props (recognised by an asset tag containing "Text", or as a titled prop with no content type) whose title is the text shown in the room, members of the group because they carry its tags (an untagged sign is invisible to these tools); each { propId, text } — and props — only the props that can hold content (presentation boards included, flagged), each as a compact entry: id, name (what the prop SHOWS: its own title, else the title of its FIRST resource, else the asset's catalog name, else the bare id when nothing names it — an id-only name means an empty, unnamed frame), assetTitle, type, thumbnailCount, logoCount, invokeType, isPresentationBoard, acceptsContent (true = type non-empty and not a presentation board), contentCount, navIndex, tag. Match the user's words against group tags/label first ("the team wall on floor 0" -> tags contain team and floor0), then against prop name/assetTitle when they mean one exact prop. Pass group ids to paste-resources-into-prop-group; when the user's content is coarser than the groups ("team" over per-floor team groups) pass every group whose tags contain the facet. The ready-made `tag` on each prop is pasted verbatim when linking to it — never assemble one. propOrder says where the order came from ({ source: "storyline" | "props-group", storylineId?, storylineTitle? }).

intents.description: Spreads existing CMS resources across the props of one or more prop GROUPS (ids from get-room-prop-groups), in the room's navigation order, as contiguous, order-preserving shares — one slideshow per prop. The tool does ALL the chunking (7 resources over 3 frames -> 3/2/2; 2 over 5 -> the first two frames get one each), so call it ONCE per content group with all of that group's resources — never once per prop, and never split the resources yourself. Pass several groupIds when the content is coarser than the room's groups (e.g. "team" photos over "building1+floor0+team" and "building1+floor1+team"); their props are pooled in walk order. Frames that still show only their template placeholder come FIRST (lowest navIndex first), frames that already hold user content come after — so a later top-up fills the empty slots before joining existing slideshows; each placement reports hadUserContent (true/false, null when the prop's content could not be read). distribution: "spread" (default — contiguous shares), "stack" (everything onto the first eligible prop as one slideshow — only when the user explicitly asked for a single slideshow) or "replicate" (EVERY resource onto EVERY eligible prop — the default when every selected group is a LOGO group, isLogoGroup true, so all logos show on all logo frames; never spread logos unless the user asks). Presentation boards are skipped automatically and listed in skippedProps; decorative members (walls, signs) are never candidates. Per prop this behaves exactly like paste-resources-into-prop: resources are link-copied (originals stay), a resource already on the prop (itself or as a link copy) is skipped rather than duplicated (per placement and top-level skippedAlreadyPresent — a repeat after a timeout is safe), template placeholder stubs are removed first, the auto content slider is enabled when a prop ends up with more than one item, and titles are cleared on EVERY content prop of the selected groups — the pasted ones and the untouched ones alike (content props carry no caption; the section's name lives on its sign; clearedTitlePropIds lists them, titleClearErrors any that failed). Returns { roomId, groupIds, distribution, placements: [{ groupId, propId, name, tag, navIndex, hadUserContent, resourceIds, addedResourceIds, failed, removedTemplateStubs, sliderEnabled, titleCleared, sliderError?, titleClearError?, stubCleanupError?, error? }], clearedTitlePropIds, titleClearErrors?, unplacedResourceIds (resources that landed on no prop at all), eligiblePropCount, skippedProps } — each placement's name and tag are read back AFTER the paste, so they name what the prop now shows (its first resource), not the empty frame it was. It throws only when nothing could be attempted: an unknown group id (the message lists the valid ids), no eligible prop in the selected groups, or empty input. Report failed/unplaced items honestly; paste each placement's `tag` verbatim when linking. Use paste-resources-into-prop only when the user named exactly one prop.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room the groups belong to.

required.name: groupIds
required.description: One or more prop group ids from get-room-prop-groups (e.g. ["building1+floor0+team"]). Several ids pool their props into one navigation-ordered row.

required.name: resourceIds
required.description: CMS resource ids to place, in display order. The tool splits them across the props itself.

optional.name: distribution
optional.description: "spread": contiguous, order-preserving shares across the eligible props in navigation order (default for every group except logo groups). "stack": everything onto the first eligible prop as a single slideshow — only when the user asked for one. "replicate": every resource onto every eligible prop (default for a logo group). Omit to get the default for the selected groups.

optional.name: appendToListEnd
optional.description: When true (default) new resources are appended to the end of each prop's content list; when false they are inserted at the front.

optional.name: removeTemplateStubs
optional.description: When true (default) placeholder resources a prop inherited from the room template are removed before pasting. Pass false only when the user explicitly wants to keep the template content.

optional.description: Network ID the room belongs to. Defaults to the current network.

Use it in the guided build once the section's name is settled (listed by the user up front, self-evident from the tag, or confirmed from your proposal — or chosen by you when the user asked you to decide everything). services.title: Room Zones Service
services.description: Zones of a room and the claims on them (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-room-claiming-zones-design.md). A zone is an invisible box in a room: it can join its video call when someone walks in, it can be claimed as somebody's personal space, or both. A CLAIM IS A PROP INVITATION on the master server — there is no other store — so the occupant also gets edit rights on the zone prop. The server does not enforce exclusivity: the earliest claim wins and the loser is withdrawn, so always read the occupancy back rather than assuming a claim held.

intents.description: Every zone of a room: {status: "ok", zones}. Each zone carries id (the prop id), title, its box in room metres (x, z, rotY in degrees, width, depth, height, floorOffset), the two capabilities (call, claim) and its claim policy (settings.audience is "members" or "listed"). A room with no zones returns an empty list.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room whose zones to list.

optional.name: claimableOnly
optional.description: Only the zones that can be claimed (the "spaces"). Default false.

intents.description: Who holds the room's claimable zones right now: {status: "ok", occupancy} keyed by zone id, each {claim, conflicts, stale}. `claim` is null when the zone is free, else {userId, claimedAt, source, doorPolicy, displayName, status}. `stale` means the occupant no longer has access to the room, so the zone is effectively free. `conflicts` are losing claims a moderator should clear. This reads the server every time — there is no push for prop invitations.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room to read.

intents.description: Claims a zone for the SIGNED-IN user. Returns {status: "ok", claim} when it worked, or {status: "refused", reason, message} when it did not — "taken", "limit", "not-listed", "not-claimable", "no-access" or "cooldown". A user who may not write prop invitations at all gets {status: "refused", reason: "needs-request"}: they must ask a room owner to assign it instead. Never claims on behalf of somebody else — use assign-zone for that.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room the zone belongs to.

required.name: zoneId
required.description: The zone to claim (its prop id, as list-room-zones returns it).

optional.name: displayName
optional.description: What to call the space, shown instead of the claimant's name.

optional.name: status
optional.description: A one-line status shown next to the space, e.g. "in focus until 4".

optional.name: doorPolicy
optional.description: Who may come in: "open" (default), "knock" or "closed". Shown, not yet enforced.

intents.description: Releases the signed-in user's own claim on a zone: {status: "ok"}. Starts a one-minute cooldown before the same user may claim that zone again. Releasing a zone somebody else holds is not possible here — a room owner uses assign-zone or the Spaces app.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room the zone belongs to.

required.name: zoneId
required.description: The zone to release.

intents.description: Gives a zone to a particular user. Requires the caller to OWN the room (manage rights) or be a network admin; anything less is refused. Bypasses the zone's audience, the room's per-user limit and the cooldown by design — this is how offices are handed out. Returns {status: "ok"}.

required.name: roomId
required.description: The room the zone belongs to.

required.name: zoneId
required.description: The zone to assign.

required.name: userId
required.description: Who gets it.

intents.description: Sends a text message to a text-chat channel. You must provide EITHER a channelId (preferred when you already have one) OR a userId (for a direct message — the service resolves the direct channel automatically). Silent — does NOT open the TextChat application, does NOT change the active channel, does NOT affect any UI. Encryption is handled automatically if the channel is encrypted.

required.description: The message body to send.

optional.name: channelId
optional.description: Target channel ID. Use this when you already know the channel (e.g. from a platform event). Takes precedence over userId.

optional.name: userId
optional.description: Target user ID for a direct message. The service resolves the direct channel by calling channel:getDirectChannel under the hood. Ignored if channelId is also provided.

optional.name: buttons
optional.description: Optional interactive buttons rendered below the message body. Pass a real JSON array (NOT a JSON-stringified array). Each entry MUST be an object with this exact NESTED shape: `{text: string, intent: {applicationId: string, action: string, params?: object}}`. Do NOT flatten `applicationId`/`action` onto the button itself — `intent` is a sub-object. `text` is the visible label. Clicking dispatches `intent` via Application.run on the recipient's client (use an `applicationId` + `action` the recipient's app exposes — see other service manifests for valid pairs). Entries that are malformed are repaired-or-dropped by the service and reported back in `buttonWarnings`; check that field on the response and use the canonical shape going forward. Example: `[{"text":"Open profile","intent":{"applicationId":"valuguru","action":"open-agent","params":{"agentId":"agent_xxx"}}}]`.

optional.name: customParams
optional.description: Optional message customParams. Only the key `open-thread` is accepted (any other key is dropped by the service). Pass `{"open-thread": true}` ONLY when the recipient explicitly expects your outreach (e.g. you are responding to their team-member avatar click) — it force-opens the chat thread on their screen, which is invasive.

intents.description: Delivers a message authored by the AI agent itself (NOT by the logged-in user) into a user's dedicated agent-to-user channel, resolved from source `userAIAgent:{userId}:{agentId}`. This is the INVASIVE owner-notification channel: use it to ping/notify the owner (pass the owner's userId) — or, occasionally, any other user. Unlike send-message (which sends as the logged-in user), this is authored by the agent. Silent toward the UI — does NOT open the TextChat application or change the active channel.

services.title: Time Service
services.description: Returns the current user's local clock context — local ISO with offset, UTC ISO for the same instant, IANA timezone, offset in minutes, day-of-week, and resolved locale. Use this before any "today"/"tomorrow"/"now" reasoning or when converting natural-language times to ISO strings.

intents.description: Returns an object describing the user's current local time: { iso: local ISO 8601 with offset (e.g. "2026-05-28T13:45:30.000+02:00"), utcIso: same instant in UTC (e.g. "2026-05-28T11:45:30.000Z"), timezone: IANA name (e.g. "Europe/Berlin"), offsetMinutes: integer minutes ahead of UTC (e.g. 120), dayOfWeek: long English day name (e.g. "Thursday"), localDate: "YYYY-MM-DD" in local time, localTime: "HH:MM" in local time, locale: resolved BCP 47 locale (e.g. "en-US") }. Takes no parameters.
